name: Burchell's Starling
rangeDescription: Southern angola to western zambia, namibia, mozambique, and northern south africa
description: A large, long-tailed, iridescent blue-green to purple glossy starling with barred wings, and a round-tipped tail. Pairs, groups, and small flocks are resident in dry savanna, especially near thorn trees, where they have become common in camps and often associate with humans.

name: Northern Silvery-Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Central philippines (bohol, samar, and leyte)
description: A small, dashing kingfisher of forested lowland streams in the central Philippines. Overall dark blue in color, more purplish on the underparts, with a creamy throat, a cream-colored spot behind the cheek, an orange spot behind the nostril, a white belly, a pale silvery-blue stripe down the back to the tail, and whitish flecks on the head and wing.

name: Red-collared Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Northern australia (kimberley region to gulf of carpenteria)
description: Large lorikeet. Very colorful, with a bright orange breast and neck, blue/black belly and head, and red bill.

name: Brown-backed Scrub-Robin
rangeDescription: Locally in southern cameroon; northwestern angola to western kenya and northwestern tanzania
description: Pretty robin with a dark brown back, a boldly marked face, and an unstreaked gray chest. Found in broadleaf woodland, moist savanna, and lush cultivation.

name: White-breasted Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Brachystegia woodland of sub-saharan africa
description: Large, chunky, gray cuckooshrike with white underparts. There is a pale ring around the dark eye, giving the face a gentle appearance.

name: Costa Rican Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Highlands of southwestern costa rica and western panama (chiriquí)
description: Medium-sized sparrowlike bird with green back, gray eyebrow, black cheek, and white throat. Most similar to Black-striped Sparrow but with entire cheek black (not just eyeline); also compare with Chestnut-capped Brushfinch but note lack of rufous crown.

name: Forest Bittern
rangeDescription: New guinea, including salawati (raja ampat islands, northwest of new guinea), and aru islands (off southwestern new guinea)
description: A large, shy bird of forest streams in the lowlands and foothills. Strong barring apart from white belly.

name: Gorgeted Sunangel
rangeDescription: Andes of southwestern colombia (nariño) and northwestern ecuador
description: Unmistakable; glittering pinkish-purple throat is distinctive in good light, but also note the snowy white chest band, which is always obvious. Medium-sized with a rather short, straight bill.

name: Black-crowned Pitta
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northern borneo
description: Dazzling pitta of Borneo’s lowland dipterocarp forests. Midnight blue above and blinding scarlet below, with a dark head, bright blue wing coverts, and a glowing silver line trailing backwards behind the eye.

name: Sakhalin Grasshopper Warbler
rangeDescription: Sakhalin, southern kuril islands, and hokkaido; winters in philippines
description: A nondescript songbird that skulks in taiga undergrowth, where very difficult to see well. Breeds on Hokkaido, Sakhalin Island, and the Kuril Islands.

name: Berlepsch's Canastero
rangeDescription: Andes of western bolivia (nevado illampu region in la paz)
description: Short-tailed canastero endemic to the Sorata vicinity in northern Bolivia. Prefers montane scrub on hillsides, but occasionally near human development and open Polylepis forest.

name: Bonaparte's Gull
rangeDescription: Northern north america; winters to mexico and greater antilles
description: The most common small gull through most of North America, especially inland. Breeding adults have a black head, thin white eye arcs, bright red legs, light gray upperparts, and black wingtips.

name: Helmeted Hornbill
rangeDescription: Myanmar to southern thailand, malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Bizarre-looking bird, now very rare due to poaching for the ivory-like material of its bill. When perched, its most recognizable feature is the naked throat pouch which resembles an undercooked steak, chalky white in the female and dull scarlet in the male.

name: Purple-crowned Plovercrest
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina (misiones) to southern brazil
description: Medium-sized charismatic hummingbird with an iridescent green body and short, straight bill. Males have a violet-blue crest and are violet below with light gray flanks.

name: Orange-winged Pytilia
rangeDescription: Central ethiopia and southern south sudan, uganda, rwanda, burundi, southern republic of the congo (lower congo river valley), southern democratic republic of the congo, tanzania, angola, zambia, and malawi southward to far northeastern namibia, northern and eastern botswana, northeastern south africa (limpopo), and south-central mozambique
description: Unusual and pretty member of the waxbill family. Shows fine olive-green barring below, yellow edges to the wing feathers, and red on the tail.

name: Spix's Spinetail
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to eastern paraguay, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Medium-sized spinetail found in light woodland, savanna, grassland, and forest edges. Note the gray-brown body contrasting with a rufous crown and wing coverts, and a black throat.

name: Grauer's Warbler
rangeDescription: Dense montane forest of eastern democratic republic of the congo, southwestern uganda, and western rwanda
description: Taxonomically unusual though not very boldly marked warbler. In poor light, or at a distance, looks dingy overall.

name: Sakalava Rail
rangeDescription: Sakalava region of northwestern madagascar (status unknown)
description: Small, rare rail that is unlikely to be seen unless you’re expressly looking for it at a handful of known sites. Cleanly rich brown on the back and gray below, with a bright yellow bill and red legs.

name: Bourke's Parrot
rangeDescription: Locally in acacia scrub of interior of southern australia
description: Small pale parrot of inland Australia woodlands, often found in mulga and acacia scrubland. Gray-brown scaly upperparts set off by unique pastel pink underparts and blue underwing and rump.

name: Broad-billed Fairywren
rangeDescription: Northern new guinea (bird's head peninsula to sepik river), including salawati (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: A small rare, and very little-known bird of treefall gaps in lowland and foothill primary forest. Pale blue underparts, deeper blue back and brownish wing.
